newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam buys 7 fuel oil, 5 gasoline cargoes for 1Q.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam buys 7 fuel oil, 5 gasoline cargoes for 1Q.

text.p: State-owned Vietnam National Petroleum Import-Export Corp (Petrolimex) has bought by tender seven cargoes of fuel oil and five cargoes of gasoline for January-March deliveries, an industry source said on Tuesday.

The 27,000-tonne cargoes of 170-centistoke, 3.0-percent sulphur fuel oil were purchased at premiums of $8.25 and $8.50 per tonne to Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Ho Chi Minh City.
Singapore trader Hin Leong was awarded five cargoes, while European major Shell and Dutch trader Vitol were awarded a cargo each.
In its last tender for October-December 1996 delivery, Petrolimex bought six fuel oil cargoes at $8.20 and $8.70 per tonne above Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f Ho Chi Minh City.

In the first quarter tender, Vietnam also bought 83-octane gasoline with a lead content of 0.15 gram per litre at a premium of 50 cents per barrel to Singapore naphtha quotes, c-and-f Hongai, Danang and Ho Chi Minh City.
Each cargo of Russian origin is 17,000 tonnes in size. The three winners were Daxin and Japanese trader Mitsui with two cargoes each, and western trader Trafigura with one cargo.
Petrolimex had initially called for nine gasoline cargoes in this tender.
But the source said Petrolimex would take delivery of two cargoes from Mitsui in the first quarter, which was originally scheduled for arrival in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Petrolimex had bought six gasoline cargoes in its fourth quarter tender at the same premium of 50 cents per barrel to Singapore naphtha quotes, c-and-f.
The source said cargoes from Singapore were offered at a premium of more than $2.00 per barrel to Singapore naphtha quotes, c-and-f basis. Vietnam did not take any Singapore cargoes, the source said.
